items.title: The Sanaa Palimpsest: The Transmission of the Qur'an in the First Centuries AH
items.venue: Oxford University Press / Institute of Ismaili Studies
items.note: Edition of DAM 01-27.1 that reads the lower text as possibly a teaching or exercise text rather than a complete rival codex.

items.title: The Qur'an: A Historical-Critical Introduction
items.note: Historical-critical introduction that weighs early-closure and later-codification views of the rasm, broadly favouring closure in the mid-seventh century.

items.title: Codex Amrensis 1
items.note: Reconstruction and edition of an early Hijazi-script codex whose leaves are dispersed among Cairo, Paris, St Petersburg and other collections.

items.title: In Search of Ali Ibn Abi Talib's Codex: History and Traditions of the Earliest Copy of the Qur'an
items.note: Studies Sunni and Shi'i reports about ʿAli's codex, one of the companion codices the tradition sets against the ʿUthmanic recension.

items.title: Le Coran, une histoire plurielle: Essai sur la formation du texte coranique
items.note: Argues from early manuscripts that the written text took shape through a longer, plural process that continued into the Umayyad period.

items.title: "The Grace of God" as evidence for a written Uthmanic archetype: the importance of shared orthographic idiosyncrasies
items.note: Shows that early manuscripts share arbitrary spellings best explained by descent from one written archetype.

items.title: Radiocarbon (14C) Dating of Qurʾān Manuscripts
items.who: M. J. Marx and T. J. Jocham
items.venue: Brill (Qurʾān Quotations Preserved on Papyrus Documents)
items.note: Reports the Corpus Coranicum radiocarbon programme, with seventh-century ranges for several Hijazi-script codices, and discusses its interpretive limits.

items.title: Arabe 334a. A Vocalized Kufic Quran in a Non-canonical Hijazi Reading
items.note: Edits a BnF manuscript whose vocalization records a non-canonical, probably Medinan reading on the standard rasm, separating rasm fixity from reading variety.

items.title: Digital Humanities and Qurʾānic Manuscript Studies: New Perspectives and Challenges for Collaborative Spaces and Plural Views
items.venue: Journal of College of Sharia and Islamic Studies
items.note: Reviews imaging, text encoding and phylogenetic approaches to early manuscripts and argues for collaborative digital editions.

items.title: The Ṣanʿāʾ Palimpsest: Materializing the Codices
items.note: Codicological study of how the lower and upper codices of the Sanaa palimpsest were made, bearing on the status of its non-ʿUthmanic text.

items.title: On the Regionality of Qurʾānic Codices
items.venue: Journal of the International Qur'anic Studies Association 5
items.note: Matches variants in early manuscripts to the regional codices described in the tradition, supporting a stemma of regionally distributed copies.

items.title: From Coptic to Arabic: A New Palimpsest and the Early Transmission History of the Qurʾān
items.venue: Journal of the International Qur'anic Studies Association 5
items.note: Publishes a newly identified palimpsest whose Qurʾān text was copied over an erased Coptic manuscript, adding a witness to early copying practice.

items.title: Quranic Arabic: From its Hijazi Origins to its Classical Reading Traditions
items.note: Reconstructs the language of the rasm from early manuscripts and reading traditions, locating it in the Hijaz.

items.title: Creating the Qur'an: A Historical-Critical Study
items.note: Argues for standardization under ʿAbd al-Malik and al-Ḥajjāj and questions whether radiocarbon dates can fix the text earlier.

items.title: QurCan: The Canonisation of the Quranic Reading Traditions
items.note: ERC grant (2023–2027, €2.0 million) on how the canonical reading traditions took shape over the standard consonantal text; concerns readings more than the rasm itself.

items.title: Radiocarbon dating of manuscripts kept in the Central Library of the University of Tehran
items.who: A. Aghaei, A. Bahrololoumi, I. Hajdas et al.
items.note: Adds a dated Kufic parchment Qurʾān fragment to the Corpus Coranicum dating campaign through the Irankoran project.

items.title: Consonantal Dotting and the Oral Quran
items.venue: Journal of the American Oriental Society
items.note: Statistical study of dotting differences among the canonical readings finds distinct Medinan, Meccan-Basran and Kufan oral traditions alongside the written rasm.

items.title: Consonantal Dotting in Early Qurʾānic Manuscripts: a Fully Dotted Qurʾān Fragment from the First/Seventh Century
items.venue: The Qurʾan and Its Handwritten Transmission (ed. F. Déroche, Brill)
items.note: Presents a fully dotted fragment assigned to the first Islamic century, evidence that diacritic practice could be systematic very early.

items.title: Scepticism as method in the study of Quranic origins: A review article of Stephen J. Shoemaker, Creating the Qur'an
items.note: Critical review of the case for an early eighth-century Marwanid canon and of the methodological scepticism behind it.
